identity.definition: A consumer-facing skincare term commonly used to point toward Centella asiatica or Centella-derived ingredients. The exact ingredient-list declaration and extract version still need to be identified.

preferred: Use the exact Centella declaration shown on the product ingredient list
label_terms.rule: Treat Cica as a category cue, not a complete ingredient identity. Do not infer plant part, extraction process, standardization, amount, or evidence match from the front label alone.

identity_boundaries: The consumer term Cica is not by itself an exact ingredient-list declaration.
One displayed Centella name may not disclose plant part, extraction process, ratio, solvent, or standardization.
Evidence for one defined extract cannot automatically support every product carrying Cica on the front.

visual_system.actor: A three-leaf Centella source silhouette with one central vein system, one extract droplet, and an incomplete version ring.
visual_system.tactile_signature: Rain-fresh rounded leaves, soft paper ground, restrained botanical translucency, and a precise liquid highlight.
motion_grammar: Draw stems first, unfold leaves from their bases, then land the extract droplet.
Use one calm botanical breath rather than decorative floating leaves.
Complete the version ring only when exact product-specific information is available.

assets.notes: Harvested from the existing ingredient-photography catalog. Keep the unbranded master unchanged; add SeoulHabit signet in the composition when needed.

avoid: treating possible label wording as universally interchangeable

components.purpose: Provide a persistent botanical recognition cue while keeping exact extract identity visibly unresolved.

safe_default: Cica is a consumer-facing cue; check the exact ingredient declaration on the product.
Product-specific information is needed to identify plant part, extraction process, standardization, and amount.
A familiar ingredient name does not make two finished formulas equivalent.
requires_context: Any efficacy, soothing, redness, barrier, collagen, or wrinkle claim requires a traceable record tied to a defined material and route.
Any percentage claim must state exactly what the percentage refers to and where the information comes from.

story_slots.purpose: Open on the familiar Cica cue while withholding a product verdict.
Connect Cica to the exact ingredient-list declaration.
avoid: treating the consumer term as the final identity

story_slots.purpose: Show which product-specific variables remain undisclosed.
Prevent category recognition from becoming a formula or efficacy conclusion.

format_input.boundary_card: Cica identifies a direction, not a standardized extract or finished-formula verdict.

gaps.reason: The visual foundation is reusable, but efficacy claims must remain unavailable until evidence records are reviewed and scoped.
gaps.build_when: before a Centella efficacy or mechanism story enters production

gaps.reason: The actor raises the version question, but the ingredient pack does not yet own a standalone process comparison.
gaps.build_when: a second story needs to compare defined Centella extracts

gaps.reason: Label-literacy stories can use the shared neutral package shell; a dedicated Centella container is not yet justified.
gaps.build_when: two formats require a Centella-specific unbranded product archetype
